headline: The new head of the Wikimedia Foundation said Wikipedia page views fell 8% last year and that some AI companies that use its content will not pay for it.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a clear first-hand statement, but one outlet and the numbers are Wikimedia's own.
importance_line: What changed: Wikipedia's chief reported an 8% fall in page views, which Axios links to AI, and said some AI firms will not pay for its content, which affects Wikipedia's readers, volunteers and donors first, then the foundation, then AI companies, and the doubt is that the 8% fall is Wikimedia's own figure for one year and the article does not show AI is the only cause.
summary: Axios reports, in an article carried by Yahoo Finance, that Wikipedia page views fell 8% in 2025, a fall Axios links to AI tools giving people Wikipedia-based answers without a visit to the site, and that Wikimedia Foundation chief executive Bernadette Meehan says some AI companies that rely heavily on its content will not pay for it. OpenAI and Anthropic are not among Wikimedia's publicly named paying customers, though Meehan said it has other agreements it did not name.
notes: Read in full. The article is Axios content syndicated by Yahoo Finance; credit Axios in the text. The interview date is not stated. Figures (8% fall, 10% of operating expenses from enterprise customers, about 80% of budget from small donations) are Wikimedia's, as relayed by Axios.
